subject.title: [Bug]: Feishu streaming card full-content updates cause severe latency regression on long replies

question: Should Feishu streaming cards add an opt-in append/transport mode for deployments where full-content CardKit updates are too slow, or should OpenClaw keep full-content-only behavior and pursue a proven cadence/backpressure fix instead?
rationale: Current main preserves full content to avoid truncation, but the latest live repro says cadence-only coalescing did not resolve the long-reply latency; choosing between an append-capable mode and full-content-only behavior changes Feishu product policy and config surface.

options.title: Decide an opt-in append/transport mode
options.body: Keep full-content as the default but allow a Feishu owner-approved opt-in mode for deployments that prove full-content CardKit updates are too slow and append semantics work correctly.

options.title: Keep full-content only
options.body: Reject append mode for now and require a replacement cadence, queueing, or backpressure fix with live Feishu proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Decline streaming-card mitigation
options.body: Document streaming=false or raw render mode as the supported workaround and close the issue only if maintainers accept the long-reply latency tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Decide an opt-in append/transport mode
recommendation.body: Keep full-content as the default but allow a Feishu owner-approved opt-in mode for deployments that prove full-content CardKit updates are too slow and append semantics work correctly.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata declares this handle as the community owner for @openclaw/feishu, and the decision is Feishu channel-specific.
